title: Swarm: guarded backup restore behind --confirm-destructive (GAP #11)
description: swarm `backup restore` used to be a hard refusal; batch 3 makes it a REAL restore behind an explicit --confirm-destructive flag (on top of --yes). SwarmAdapter.BackupRestoreAsync refuses without ConfirmDestructive (pointing at the DR runbook), and with it uploads the take's consul.snap / nomad.snap to a manager and runs `consul snapshot restore` + `nomad operator snapshot restore` online against the leader, counting restored Consul KV keys + Nomad jobs. Step 1 proves the guard (refused, exit 2). Step 2 proves the GREEN path by taking a fresh snapshot and restoring THAT SAME snapshot in place -- an idempotent self-restore (identical KV/jobs), exactly what was live-verified 2026-07-06. DESTRUCTIVE by design: it overwrites live Consul KV + Nomad job state (here with identical data). Recovering an ISOLATED cluster from a DIFFERENT backup follows the DR runbook (handbook 3).

prerequisites.smokeGate: nexus-infra-swarm-nomad smoke-0.E.4e ALL GREEN; pwsh on PATH (step 2 captures the take's backupId); Consul/Nomad ACL bootstrap tokens seeded in Vault KV

observe.what: REFUSED before touching the cluster: 'swarm restore OVERWRITES the live Consul KV + Nomad job state in place -- refused without an explicit opt-in. Re-run with --confirm-destructive (in addition to --yes) ...'. Exit 2. The guard fires ahead of the backup-id lookup, so even a bogus id is refused.

steps.command: pwsh -NoProfile -Command "$j=(nexus backup take swarm --tag restoredemo --json | ConvertFrom-Json).backupId; Write-Host TAKE=$j; nexus backup restore swarm $j --yes --confirm-destructive; exit $LASTEXITCODE"

observe.what: TAKE=swarm-restoredemo-<timestamp> (the id from the fresh take), then a GREEN 'backup restore swarm-restoredemo-...' rule with 'items restored : N' = restored Consul KV keys + Nomad jobs. The consul/nomad snapshot restore ran online against the leader.

observe.where: ssh nexusadmin@<swarm-manager> 'export CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR=... ; consul kv export | grep -c key'
observe.what: the Consul KV key count matches the restored count -- the restore actually replaced state (with the identical fresh snapshot)

whatProves: swarm backup restore is a real, guarded, online restore: refused without --confirm-destructive (exit 2, no cluster change), and with it runs consul + nomad snapshot restore against the leader and reports the restored item count. The extra opt-in prevents an accidental in-place overwrite of the live orchestration tier.
